thesis: The bear carries the normalised-earnings objection because pricing dominates sequential growth and the proposed mix resilience has no contract/cash proof. Neutral preserves verified datacenter and revenue growth without predicting a NAND reversal. Peak net earnings and the low forward estimate are unsuitable sustainable-value anchors.
strongest_counterexample: FY revenue grew175%, datacenter revenue437% and ten agreements were signed, providing genuine customer-mix opportunity beyond a claim that all demand is merely pricing.
invalidation_conditions: Verified agreement/pricing disclosures show comparable earnings and FCF above zero during a subsequent observed NAND-price decline, directly testing and potentially overturning the unresolved cycle-resilience objection.
A comparable annual datacenter revenue growth rate at or below zero with declining prices would invalidate the retained mix-growth counterweight.
evidence_gaps: Contract economics, NAND price/volume decomposition and through-cycle cash.
Tax/nonrecurring earnings reconciliation, debt and FCF.
Normalised valuation and corporate-action/predecessor comparability of413-bar history.
decisive_factors: Approximately two-thirds of sequential growth came from pricing.
Residual one-third is not verified unit growth.
$6.90bn GAAP net income needs normalisation; cooling MACD and short-history caveat.
